💡 Key Takeaways
  • Both male and female kelp were shown to be capable of reproduction without fertilization.Credit: Madelein_Wolf/Getty.
  • When potential mates are scarce, some types of seaweed can take reproduction into their own hands, so to speak, according to a study published on 12 November in PLoS Biology1.
  • “Our findings highlight that kelp are even more flexible in their reproduction than previously appreciated,” notes Daniel Liesner, a marine biologist at the GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel in Germany.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Both male and female kelp were shown to be capable of reproduction without fertilization.Credit: Madelein_Wolf/Getty.

When potential mates are scarce, some types of seaweed can take reproduction into their own hands, so to speak, according to a study published on 12 November in PLoS Biology1.

“Our findings highlight that kelp are even more flexible in their reproduction than previously appreciated,” notes Daniel Liesner, a marine biologist at the GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel in Germany.

The brown algae, which provide food and shelter for marine life, “are really weird, they do all kinds of stuff”, indicates Reina Veenhof, an ecologist at the Scottish Association for Marine Science in Oban, UK. What’s interesting about the study is that it helps to explain how changes in gene activity allow kelp to reproduce in different ways, she says.

Scientists know that kelp can reproduce asexually, with unfertilized eggs developing into offspring. This process was even documented for one male strain2 — the PLoS Biology study shows that this wasn’t a one-off.

It has been revealed that the ability of male reproductive cells to develop without fertilization is striking, states Olivier De Clerck, a seaweed biologist at Ghent University in Belgium. This is because, unlike eggs, sperm cells are small and have few resources to support development.

Sources indicate that the researchers focused on Laminaria pallida, a species found along the Atlantic coasts of South Africa and Namibia. In the wild, 523 individual kelp showed no clear evidence of asexual reproduction.

By contrast, both microscopic male and female L. pallida grown in separate laboratory dishes could produce offspring without fertilization. During asexual reproduction, the gene expression in males changed, making them more similar to females.

However, when they were lab-grown in the presence of a member of the opposite sex, kelp favoured sexual reproduction, suggesting they can detect nearby partners through chemical signals.

Chelsea have emerged as the most likely Premier League destination for Alessandro Bastoni if the Inter Milan defender decides to leave Serie A in 2027.

The Italy international is widely regarded as one of Europe’s leading centre-backs, and his representatives are now assessing potential options amid uncertainty over his long-term future at San Siro.

Liverpool remain serious admirers, while other leading European clubs have also monitored Bastoni, but Chelsea’s interest appears particularly strong as Xabi Alonso looks to strengthen his defensive options.

According to TEAMtalk, Chelsea have already been spoken to about Bastoni and are regarded as his most likely destination in England if he chooses the Premier League.

Chelsea representatives were also reportedly present to watch the 27-year-old during Italy’s recent 3-1 victory over France, where he produced another impressive performance.

Liverpool have been kept informed of developments, although centre-back is right now considered less urgent for the Reds following their recent investment in younger defenders.

Inter, meanwhile, want to extend Bastoni’s contract beyond its current 2028 expiry date.

Failure to reach an agreement could make next summer increasingly important, as the Italian club would have to decide whether to cash in before his contractual position begins to weaken.

Sources indicate that bastoni is left-footed, composed under pressure and exceptional at progressing possession from defence. Perhaps most importantly, he has years of experience operating in a back three, making him an obvious tactical fit for Alonso.

As per recent reports, Chelsea and Liverpool were tracking Bastoni and that Inter valued their defender at around £70million.

That is a substantial fee for a player who will be 28 next year, but Chelsea’s squad arguably needs experience as much as it needs potential.

The Blues have invested heavily in young defenders, yet adding someone who has competed consistently at the highest levels of Serie A and the Champions League could provide greater stability.

The major challenge will be convincing Bastoni.

Industry observers note that he has been comfortable at Inter for years and will not leave simply because a Premier League club offers more money. His camp reportedly wants any future manager to be fully committed to signing him.

For Chelsea, that should not be an matter. If Alonso believes Bastoni can become the leader of his defence, the club should make that message clear and put themselves at the front of the queue.

#13766. Thomas Tuchel is now embracing traditional English values - clarity has helped England understand who they are, and now they can beat the best, writes CRAIG HOPE

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (935 w)
📖 Baca

Thomas Tuchel is now embracing traditional English values - clarity has helped England understand who they are, and now they can beat the best, writes CRAIG HOPE

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (935 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:57 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 16:57 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • According to recent reports, thomas Tuchel has always liked what he sees from his England players on the training pitch.
  • It is why, when the squad reconvened at St George’s Park in September, Tuchel used the meeting room as much as he did the grass to address that disparity in delivery.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 16:57 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 16:57 EST, 16 November 2026.

According to recent reports, thomas Tuchel has always liked what he sees from his England players on the training pitch. Less so, at times, inside a stadium. It is a contradiction with which he has wrestled since the World Cup, when performances on the whole left him underwhelmed, save for the collective spirit and individual excellence that rescued results.

It is why, when the squad reconvened at St George’s Park in September, Tuchel used the meeting room as much as he did the grass to address that disparity in delivery.

At the same time, the elephant in the corner of the auditorium was the German’s own comments about the DNA of English players compared to the likes of Spain, and fundamentally them lacking the coding to protect possession and, therefore, valuable leads. He asked Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and others for their thoughts.

In a recent development, the message back from his players was this – let us be better at being us, not them. Interestingly, that was Tuchel’s mantra upon his appointment, one of embracing traditional English values. Amid the World Cup fallout, though, he had wandered in a daze down a rabbit hole of genetics, focusing on what his team cannot do as opposed to what they can.

Tuchel, his staff and his players are tacticians and technicians, not scientists. If the intricacies of DNA do not allow them to be Spain, then don’t be. Be England, they determined. That is not to say kick and rush, bark and bite. After all, Kane is officially the best player in the world right now and Bellingham, unofficially, is playing as well as anyone on the planet.

Rather, there needed to be clarity – this is what we are and this is how we beat the best. On Sunday night in Madrid, England beat the very best. It was a victory born from those hours on the training field and in conference, and even more spent by Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry during their post-tournament review in a St George’s Park war room. They knew then that this was not a case of rip it up and start again, more so mend the tears and give the likes of Bellingham a blank sheet to impact where, and how, he sees best.

Thomas Tuchel is embracing England's DNA and reaping the rewards following the World Cup.

England can now beat the best, which they showed against Spain in a fantastic victory.

Industry observers note that there was no radical strategical change, but there was a fresh doctrine, principles that should underpin whatever the in-game circumstance – off-the-ball running, a high press, filling in for a team-mate who has seized a moment to improvise elsewhere, such as the full backs. Ben White scoring England’s third on Sunday and Lewis Hall completing four more dribbles than Lamine Yamal were examples of Tuchel’s allowance for greater intuition. Be you, not Spain.

Sources indicate that kane, informally at least, has also been promoted beyond captain, a bridge between management and dressing-room. To see him in a semi-coaching and cajoling capacity on the touchline after he was taken off in the 78th minute against Spain was to witness this elevation.

But even if England had conceded a late equaliser at the Metropolitano Stadium, it would not have mattered. Not when it comes to measuring post World Cup improvement. To have drawn comparison with Argentina and that second-half collapse would have been unfair and inaccurate. The semi-final was 11 versus 11 and so let us judge this game on the same terms. And what did England do with a 1-0 lead and 11 players? They attacked. And attacked again. For all of the tweaks Tuchel and Barry have made to the structure of training and the team’s set-up, this was evidence of them learning from a mistake, as much as the head coach will be loath to admit.

Ezri Konsa, however, did reveal there was a definite instruction to keep attacking Spain when Tuchel addressed the team at half-time.

It has been revealed that ‘The instruction was to keep going at them,’ remarked the defender. ‘Don’t stop. To keep our foot on the pedal. That is what we did. Argentina was different, different circumstances. But it was not just half-time. We went 1-0 up and Harry, our captain, told us to keep going and to keep our foot on the pedal too.'.

Recent findings suggest that before Jarell Quansah’s needless mistake and Elliot Anderson’s subsequent dismissal in the 63rd minute, the game was not in the balance in any way. As a live observer of almost every Tuchel match since his arrival, this was the best performance of his reign. In fact, it’s not even close.

In a recent development, and yet, so much still comes back to Bellingham. England would not have won without him. He terrified Spain, perhaps given their intimate knowledge of his powers. Beating the best is as much a mental challenge as it is physical, and Bellingham believed. He made England believe, too. His swagger. His majesty. And yes, his skill. He won the corner for Konsa’s headed second and created the third for White. He then dropped into midfield when down to ten and battled and organised like a captain.

Bellingham has bought into the collective under Tuchel and, with that, his team-mates are buying into his big ideas. For now, they don’t come much bigger than what England achieved in Madrid.

James is a Senior Editor for GIVEMESPORT with over eight years of experience in the industry. After graduating from the University of Southampton in 2016 with a degree in history, he joined the company as an Academy member in July 2017 and, after a short time working as a freelancer, was given a full-time role in February 2018. He primarily covers the biggest stories in the football world but is also comfortable reporting on a variety of other sports including darts, golf, Formula 1, tennis, boxing and athletics. He has covered some massive events during his time at GIVEMESPORT, including numerous Champions League and World Cup finals, as well as the Olympics in 2020 and 2024.

When Ben White made his England debut in 2021, it was expected that he would play a key role for his national team for many years to come.

Recent findings suggest that however, he refused to play for his country for years after leaving England's camp during the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. The day after England's final Group B match, it was unveiled that White would be returning home due to personal reasons.

Speaking in 2024, Gareth Southgate revealed that White had informed England that he did not want to be considered for selection.

White finally returned to the fold in March 2026 when he was included in Thomas Tuchel's squad for two friendly matches ahead of the World Cup.

It has been revealed that he made his first appearance in four years against Uruguay at Wembley Stadium, coming on as a second half substitution. He was loudly booed by his own fans as he made his way onto the pitch. The Arsenal defender went on to score and give away a penalty.

It has not been made clear as to exactly why White left England's 2022 World Cup squad and made himself unavailable for selection for many years afterward.

It has been revealed that there were rumours that White had fallen out with Southgate's assistant manager, Steve Holland. Piers Morgan has now revealed the 'real reason' why White left England's camp, giving more details of his bust-up with Holland.

According to recent reports, morgan said on Football Uncensored: “My view on Ben White… he’s a fantastic player. He’s been great at Arsenal, he competes with (Jurrien) Timber for the right-back (spot) but I think he’s terrific.

“He still gets booed by a section of England fans because of what happened at the Qatar World Cup in 2022, where he had this massive falling-out with Steve Holland.

“My understanding of what happened is that Holland was mocking him in front of all the players for the supposed statement that Ben White made that he doesn’t like football.

“In fact, what he said was that he doesn’t like going home and watching football after he’s been playing it all day. And he made the point this week clarifying it, that, like a lot of people, when they finish their job for the day, they don’t want to go back home and talk about it… I totally understood that.”.

White returned to the England fold after Holland left the England set up alongside Southgate in 2024.

Morgan added: “Now the interesting thing about Holland is that he’s gone to Manchester United, he’s just been fired as part of the Carrick regime, he had a terrible year there, he fell out with all the players, especially Bruno Fernandes, who’s their only good player.

“So, for me, I’m totally team Ben White and the fact that he’s back in the England team is great and we should stop booing him.”.

White chose not to go into detail when asked what happened in Qatar and why he made himself unavailable for England selection for many years afterward.

He told the BBC: "I think obviously people don't know the full story, because I [have] never noted anything and I won't put anyone under the bus or share any of that. I think that is probably the best way.

"It's been amazing [though], obviously a bit tricky and not straightforward, but it is amazing to be here now.".

In a recent development, when asked whether he would have done anything differently, he continued: "No, I don't think I would. Obviously, I was a bit younger, I am a bit older now.

"I think as a person I am quite real and I think I made the decision that I would probably continue to make. So, one that I am not happy about, but obviously it happened and [it is] time to move on.".

White, who is one of the highest-paid English footballers, has now made eight appearances for his country. He scored his second goal for his country in the Three Lions' 3-2 victory over world champions Spain at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano Stadium in November 2026.

Sources indicate that liverpool’s interest is easy to understand. Virgil van Dijk is approaching the latter stages of his career, and the Reds need to continue identifying younger centre-backs before a major transition becomes unavoidable.

De Winter can operate in a traditional central partnership or on the right of a back three, giving him useful tactical flexibility.

United have an equally strong reason to monitor him. Pochettino is expected to strengthen at centre-back in January, and De Winter’s age, physical profile and experience at a major European club fit the type of signing United should be considering.

According to recent reports, the obstacle is Milan. De Winter is contracted until 2030 and has started 10 of their opening 11 Serie A matches, leaving the Rossoneri under no pressure to negotiate.

For both Liverpool and United, continuing to scout him makes sense. But unless Milan’s position changes dramatically, a summer approach looks considerably more realistic than paying a January premium.

"The referee's report is the only document in the disciplinary proceedings file, and the Committee must determine the sanction based solely on this information. "Furthermore, the subsequent consequences of the action, which are also documented in the referee's report and are public knowledge, have been taken into account to increase the sanction to the maximum level permitted by the regulations. Sources indicate that pique then referred to an incident in the match between Albacete and Sabadell earlier this month. It has been revealed that pique then referred to an incident involving him and former Barcelona goalkeeper Victor Valdes in 2012. In their Champions League semi-final clash against Chelsea, Pique took a blow to the head after colliding with Valdes. He had to leave the pitch and woke up in hospital. Pique said Valdes wasn't to blame and that the situation with Owono was very similar.

He finished: "And we humans often need to blame someone because, otherwise, we can't understand why this happens on the field. It's an accident. I think imposing the maximum penalty on Jesús puts him in an unfair situation, because he isn't to blame for what ended up happening.".

Manchester United have several talented youngsters in their ranks at the moment, but arguably the best of the bunch is Chido Obi.

The Danish striker hit the headlines in 2023 when he scored 10 goals for Arsenal in an under-16 match against Liverpool. Obi decided that Arsenal wasn't the best team to continue his development, though, and he signed for Man Utd in the summer of 2024.

The youngster was just 17 years old when he made his debut for the Red Devils. He went onto play eight times for the first-team in the 2024/25 campaign as he looked to make his mark in the Premier League.

After failing to make a single appearance in 2025/26, Obi joined Eredivisie outfit Willem II on a season-long loan in September. United would have hoped that he could continue his development in the Netherlands and return a much better player, but things haven't worked out as they would have hoped.

According to recent reports, three days after signing for Willem II, Obi made his debut for the club against Excelsior. He played the final eight minutes as Willem II were beaten 3-0.

Industry observers note that A few weeks later, he made his home debut for the club, coming on as a late substitute in a 5-1 defeat to Dutch giants Ajax. Obi put in a promising performance as he played a key role in his side's goal. He has failed to kick on from there, though.

Recent findings suggest that it's been a dismal campaign so far for Willem II, who are still waiting for their first win in the Eredivisie. They are currently rock bottom of the Netherlands' top tier, having picked up just three points from their opening 12 matches. They are seven points away from safety.

Despite Willem II's struggles, Obi has struggled for game-time. He has not started a single game for the club, coming on as a second-half substitute on six occasions. He has not found the back of the net in the 71 minutes he has played.

It has been revealed that he was given 24 minutes in his side's victory over Helmond in the Dutch Cup on October 27. After the match, caretaker boss Adrie Koster wasn't happy with his defensive efforts when Willem went down to ten men.

According to recent reports, koster mentioned: "It is partly a matter of mindset, but also of youthful exuberance. That boy has never experienced anything like this before. He doesn't do it on purpose either, so we shouldn't focus everything on him. This is simply part of his learning process. But we are going to talk to him about it.".

Obi's struggles have been so great that United are said to be considering recalling him in January. The Manchester Evening News report that United insert break clauses into the contracts of each young player they send on loan, and that they will consider activating the clause if Obi's situation does not improve.

According to recent reports, still only 18 years old, Obi still has time to fulfill his lofty potential. His spell in the Netherlands has been nothing short of a nightmare so far, though. It remains to be seen whether he can turn his fortunes around.

Published: 17:56 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 19:19 EST, 16 November 2026.

Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz scored a stunning brace for Germany as Jurgen Klopp's side thumped the Netherlands in the Nations League.

The 23-year-old has had a tough time of it at Anfield since his £116million move to the club last summer, but has never really struggled on the international stage.

And he continued that trend on Monday evening with two goals for his side to help them top their Nations League group.

His first was the pick of the bunch. Wirtz moved along the forward line as a Dutch side without Virgil van Dijk struggled to contain him. He picked up the ball around 25 yards out, cut inside onto his weaker left foot, and curled a pearling effort into the far corner off the post.

That goal, which came on the hour mark, put his side 2-0 up after Freiburg's Derry Scherhant had scored the opener, and Wirtz wasn't done there.

Centre back Nico Schlotterbeck made it 3-0 before the Liverpool man picked up his second of the night after drifting into the penalty box unmarked and finishing high after good work from Brajan Gruda.

Industry observers note that cette version de Wirtz avec le maillot de la Mannschaft c’est celle qu’on aimerait voir chaque semaine en PL. Quel missile pour faire le break ! Meilleur buteur allemand sur cette édition de l’UNL. 🇩🇪🔥 pic.twitter.com/m0DqaOungS.

Florian Wirtz scored a brace for Germany as they thumped the Netherlands 5-0 in Nations League action.

Liverpool midfielder Wirtz received a big hug from a smiling Jurgen Klopp at full time.

Gruda himself, who is on loan at RB Leipzig from Brighton, wrapped up the five-star win on a night that arguably saw Klopp announce himself as Germany boss.

After full-time, the ex-Liverpool manager gave Wirtz a huge hug as the duo beamed with major smiles on their faces.

While it was a night to remember for Germany, a Netherlands team that included the likes of Micky van de Ven, Jurrien Timber and Wirtz's Liverpool team-mate Cody Gakpo were left exasperated.

Van Dijk had pulled out of the squad with a knock after playing with a knock in recent weeks.

His side will still, though, compete in the Nations League quarter-finals after finishing second in the group, finishing ahead of Greece on goal difference.

As for Wirtz, he will hope his performance will help continue what has been an uphill climb so far this season.

He also found the net for Germany in their first match of the international break – a 3-1 win over Serbia – and picked up a goal and assist in Liverpool's 3-1 win over Crystal Palace before the international break.

In total, he has two goals and five assists in 15 games for Liverpool this season – though the Reds will hope those numbers increase as the season goes on.

His second goal came as he drifted into the penalty area and finished high into the net.

Last month, meanwhile, Reds manager Andoni Iraola insisted he has full faith in his midfielder.

'I think he has had a little bit of everything this season,' he said. 'He has had good games, probably the other day was not his best game, especially offensively. We trust Florian.

It has been revealed that 'Florian is a very good player. He was coming from good performances in the international break, I think. I think it is a matter of everyone to find his moment.'.

Klopp hailed him 'exceptional', meanwhile, during the last international break.

Chelsea have tracked him for several years and appear determined to keep him on their radar despite his decision to remain in Seville.

According to ABC, as relayed by Mundo Deportivo, Chelsea contacted Morante’s representatives during the summer after his impressive performances at the Under-19 European Championship.

Morante helped Spain win the competition, finishing as joint-top scorer with four goals and earning a place in the tournament’s best XI.

Chelsea’s approach did not develop into a formal bid because Morante preferred to stay with Betis and fight for first-team opportunities. The Spanish club subsequently rewarded him with a contract until 2030 containing a €30million release clause.

That decision has already produced encouraging signs. Morante scored shortly after coming on for his La Liga debut against Osasuna and has also featured in the Champions League.

His immediate concern is fitness, with an adductor concern making him doubtful for Betis’ derby against Sevilla on 21 November.

There is little surprise that Chelsea like Morante.

Sources indicate that he is young, technically gifted, comfortable on either wing and available for a relatively achievable fee if his development continues. At €30m, his release clause could eventually look extremely attractive.

The bigger question is whether Chelsea actually need another young winger.

Xabi Alonso already has significant competition in wide areas, although that picture could change in January. CaughtOffside reports that Chelsea could allow Jamie Gittens to leave temporarily after his struggle for regular first-team football.

That possibility could eventually create more space for another developing attacker, but Chelsea should resist collecting talent without offering a clear pathway.

Industry observers note that morante appears happy at Betis and has only just begun establishing himself at senior level. Leaving now could actually slow his progress.

Industry observers note that for Chelsea, the sensible approach is to continue scouting him rather than rush into activating the clause. If Morante develops into a regular La Liga performer, €30m may become difficult to ignore but only if the Blues can offer him meaningful minutes.

All 92 English football clubs, from League Two to the Championship and Premier League, have been ranked by their average attendances for the 2026/27 season so far.

Some clubs boasting the biggest stadiums haven't necessarily managed to pack out their impressive arenas, while a number of typically 'smaller' sides (for want of a better word) have punched above their weight and ranked higher than expected, thanks in part to their flying starts to the campaign.

According to recent reports, ranking at the very bottom, with an average attendance of just 1,853, are Accrington Stanley. Barnet, Fleetwood Town - who recently knocked Arsenal out of the League Cup - and Salford City, rank just above them, with the latter being owned by some of Man United's Class of 92 but still struggling to find their own identity. This comes despite sitting top of League Two and among the favourites for another promotion.

Other notable clubs who feature in this section are Grimsby Town in 72nd, who own one of the ugliest stadiums in British football, while Swindon Town - who found themselves in the topflight in the 1993/94 season - rank two places ahead, with the Robins managing just 7,608 fans at their games this season.

Oldham Athletic, York City and Blackpool are among several clubs in this section that have struggled to stay afloat in recent years, with all three coming perilously close to extinction because of financial troubles. Part of the problem may stem from the fact that none regularly attract more than 10,000 fans to home matches, although the wider state of the English game is a far bigger factor.

Recent findings suggest that despite enjoying three successive promotions over the last three seasons as they set their sights on reaching the Premier League sooner rather than later, Wrexham still have around 200 empty seats per match at present. They rank 54th on this list, behind the likes of Barnsley, Lincoln City and MK Dons.

Bournemouth's rise to prominence followed a similar path to Wrexham's, but they have yet to move away from their old, much smaller stadium. As a result, they boast the lowest average attendance of any Premier League side, ranking 51st overall, just one place above Luton Town, who have endured successive relegations in the opposite direction.

Brentford, who have to contend with the fact that several of their London neighbours boast much bigger fanbases, sit 42nd, behind Watford, Swansea City and Huddersfield Town.

Industry observers note that millwall, meanwhile, are renowned as one of the toughest clubs in English football and, alongside south London rivals Charlton Athletic, find themselves averaging just under 20,000 fans at home matches. It's a similar story for two-time FA Cup winners Portsmouth. Another side with a reputation for making plenty of noise are Stoke City, who average 22,288 in the Championship. That figure just about keeps the age-old question of 'can he do it on a cold, wet Tuesday night in Stoke?' alive and kicking.

Sources indicate that other top-flight sides in this section include Hull City in 29th, Crystal Palace in 27th and Fulham in 22nd. None of them quite manage to attract more supporters than Leicester City, however, despite the Foxes sitting 10th in the division below.

The three biggest clubs missing out on a place in the top 10 are Nottingham Forest (16th), Leeds United (13th), and Aston Villa (11th). But there is quite a jump between them and Chelsea, who just about make it in 10th with an average attendance at Stamford Bridge of 39,507.

Arsenal, top of the league as they look to retain their first Premier League title in 22 years, are surprisingly only sixth, behind both Manchester City and Liverpool. This means they also rank third in London, with Tottenham in third and West Ham in second.

But there's no surprise that Manchester United's Old Trafford, the biggest club stadium in the UK, ranks top. Fanbanter's findings suggest their attendance has increased from last term, despite the Red Devils having recently sacked Michael Carrick for Mauricio Pochettino as they sit 18th and in the relegation zone.

Multiple sources in Italy say Moise Kean’s return to action with Como has been delayed due to a upcoming tibia glitch.

Italy and Como striker Kean will be out longer than expected.

The 26-year-old last played in October, featuring in Italy’s 1-1 draw against France, and was expected to miss five weeks.

However, La Provincia di Como and Sky Sport Italia claim that Kean will need more time to recover.

According to La Provincia di Como, Kean recently saw a newly introduced specialist, while Sky claims the striker has developed new problems in his tibia.

Although the nature of his latest problem remains unclear, Kean won’t be back anytime soon, as both media outlets say the ex-Fiorentina and Juventus star needs more time to return to action.

Kean joined Como from Fiorentina in a €40m deal last summer. The Italy international scored one goal and provided one assist in six appearances before his injury.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row. Three different managers have been sacked in that time, and the mood in north London had plunged to grim lows, but finally there is a sense that something truly exciting is stirring at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be. After Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, Spurs simply had to make their numerical advantage count. They did so with relative ease, taking complete control of possession and creating endless goalscoring opportunities.

Industry observers note that roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149. The goals ultimately came from two defenders, Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke, but there was a long list of Spurs players who might have scored here.

Spurs take the lead through an Archie Gray header! ⚪ https://t.co/qSCECkOJur.

According to recent reports, did this defeat mark the end for Pierre Sage, the Palace manager? The Frenchman was only appointed in June but it has been a grisly start to the campaign. Palace have the worst defence in the league, have lost six of nine games and have not produced any truly encouraging performances in the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that even in the two games Palace have won, against Fulham and Nottingham Forest, they were lucky to do so. The likes of Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank, both of whom would be strong candidates to replace Sage if Palace do pull the trigger, will no doubt have been keeping an eye on events here.

According to recent reports, “I am really aware of the situation,” Sage remarked. “I don’t like this situation. [But] you can trust in me, I will never give up. I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. I have the rage to train more. It’s not me to decide this thing [his future]. If I have one hour, I will give my best for one hour. If I have 10 years, I will give my best for 10 years.”.

The decision for Palace chairman Steve Parish, then, is whether this result represented a continuation of the team’s problems or was an aberration caused by the early red card. It would be reasonable for Sage to claim this match was out of his hands from the moment Mateta lunged at Spurs captain Micky van de Ven, but such an argument might not carry much weight with Palace sitting 18th in the table.

Recent findings suggest that the challenge was foolish in the extreme by Mateta, a player who was much more successful in exiting this game than he has been in his numerous attempts to leave Palace in recent transfer windows. At first glance it did not seem the worst tackle, but the replays were damning: Mateta led with his studs and made forceful contact with Van de Ven’s ankle.

In a recent development, it was an inexcusably brainless act, after just 13 minutes of play, and the same could be said of Palace’s defending from a right-wing corner a few minutes later. Mohammed Kudus swirled the delivery to the back post, where Gray was unmarked. Yes, Palace were defending with 10. But no, that does not justify the inability of Sage’s players to spot Gray. Even more embarrassingly, the Tottenham player was unmarked again from another corner shortly afterwards.

Sources indicate that it was not the first time this season that Palace’s cause has been undermined by a red card. When they lost at home to Ipswich Town in September, Axel Disasi was sent off after 34 minutes. An absence of discipline? Perhaps. Sage might argue, though, that he is not responsible for his players demonstrating a lack of basic brainpower.

Industry observers note that all of this was welcomed heartily by the Spurs fans, who celebrated Mateta’s dismissal as though it was a goal. Recent results have restored some of the enthusiasm in this corner of north London and the mood here was buoyant, even before Gray’s opener.

“Now we are playing as a team,” De Zerbi said. “Before the international break, we were playing as many good players but not as a team. We revealed our maturity. We are improving.”.

The second goal was always coming and it arrived in the 73rd minute, when Van Hecke attacked a wonderful cross by Mateus Fernandes. Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson saved the first attempt but the ball dropped onto the head of Van Hecke, now seated in the six-yard box, and he happily nodded it home.

Sandro Tonali was exceptional in midfield and teenage talent Luca Williams-Barnett also sparkled off the bench. “Tonali was unbelievable,” De Zerbi noted. “We played with two players more: Tonali was double.”.

Spurs face Leeds United, Ipswich Town, Sunderland and Fulham in their next four league games. The momentum could, and perhaps should, continue to build. Their optimism here contrasted sharply with the angst of Palace, and with the troubled look that was etched on Sage’s face.

Industry observers note that “Very pleased for the performance, very tough game. You don’t know 11 [against 11] would be different game but Crystal Palace are very tough because they defend with a low block, no space and we highlighted we are a mature team. Maybe we could score more goals with more nastiness, but I am very happy because we created many chances. We need more goals for sure. It’s not enough, but we are improving a lot.

“I was very nervous before the game, during the game, after the red card, it’s always better playing with one player more. But today, against this team, they played with this behaviour, all behind the line of the ball, aggressive. Very tough game.”.

According to recent reports, when asked if Spurs are looking up the table, he replied: “We don’t forget the ambitions. We have to look behind what was the situation two weeks ago. In the last two years, two times 17th in the table, many games without a win in front of our fans. We have to stay focused. They are improving, increasing the level of performance.”.

According to recent reports, speaking to Sky Sports, the Palace defender stated: “Definitely was frustrating. It was one of the first tackles of the game. And we felt like we were doing well and it is unfortunate. We go again.

According to recent reports, “The main message was don’t concede again, stay tight as a defence and try to hit them on the counter. That is the best plan when you’re down a man.

“Unfortunately, it didn’t happen today. We know what we can do as a team, as a back five, the whole unit. There were some positives in the games, but I can’t say much when you lose. We just have to go again.

“Hopefully, the next game we win. The main message is to stay together as a team. We know what we are capable of. It is staying confident and bouncing back.”.

Barcelona came from a goal down to win the meeting of LaLiga’s top two at the Metropolitano. Giuliano Simeone gave Atlético Madrid the lead. Atlético had arrived with nine wins, one draw and one defeat from their first 11 league matches. Barcelona had scored 46 league goals in that same stretch.

Industry observers note that hansi Flick reshaped his side at half-time. Frenkie de Jong came on at right-back for Brian Fariñas. Barcelona pressed higher after the break. On 66 minutes, Lamine Yamal’s pass set up Fermín for the winner.

The result carries extra weight for Barcelona. Atlético beat them in the Champions League quarter-finals and in the Copa del Rey last season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, en route to their second NWSL championship in two years, relatively upcoming Gotham FC recruit Jaedyn Shaw was uninterested in the narratives that underestimated her team. The surprise win at the NWSL Shield-winning Kansas City Current in the playoff quarterfinals was not a surprise to her, and she made it clear with three quick words: "Underdog, my ass.".

Shaw had a point on that cold day in the Midwest, and almost exactly a year later, it still stands. Gotham are the NWSL's fresh dynasty, and their Shield win marked their fifth major title in three years, with a sixth in their sights as the playoffs begin this weekend. The transformation was rapid for a team that has historically been a bottom-dweller, so much so that their 2023 championship triumph was a genuine surprise. They rapidly built a title-winning team and reaped the rewards just as swiftly, but even as the muscle memory of title charges returns, Gotham will go about their next NWSL playoff journey differently. The target is officially on their backs, the onus officially on them to live up to the billing.

It has been revealed that gotham have played the vast majority of their playoff games as the lowest-seeded team in the postseason, winning the championship twice in those circumstances. Sunday's quarterfinal against the Seattle Reign, though, will be the first game they play as the unquestionable favorites to win the whole thing. How Gotham will play with the weight of expectations is entirely unclear, since they have never done it before, but it is a good problem of their own creation, one they have chased since the 2023 triumph.

It has been revealed that date: Sunday, Nov. 8 | Time: 12:30 p.m. ETLocation: Sports Illustrated Stadium -- Harrison, N.J.TV: ABC | Live stream: ESPN AppOdds: Gotham FC -150; Draw +265; Seattle Reign +340.

Their blitz in the free-agent market in the winter of 2024 laid the foundation for their dynastic run, but the most fascinating feature of Gotham's years-long run of success is the evolution they have undergone since. U.S. women's national team defender Tierna Davidson has become the team's captain, her progressive passing ability making her a key fixture in head coach Juan Carlos Amoros' system. Her club and country teammate Rose Lavelle has become a standout, but the star of the show has been Shaw, who has barely missed a beat since her arrival in September 2025.

Shaw has 14 goals and seven assists in 35 NWSL games with Gotham, her wide-ranging skill set fully on display in Amoros' team. She has been a little bit of everything for the team's attack, which is arguably too reliant on her talents, but it is almost hard to fault Amoros for the approach. The system has allowed Shaw to flourish, in particular bringing out a clear goal-scoring quality that is key to a Gotham team that values defensive work rate first.

In a recent development, "First, I think the commitment they have to defend and the commitment they have to work hard for the team despite being some of the best players technically in the planet," Amoros stated about both Shaw and Lavelle after a win over the Chicago Stars in September. "I think that helps the connection, not only between them two. There is a mutual respect there because of that but then also from the whole team. When you have to play and those are the players that produce the chances for us in the final third but then the people that [are] behind them are always supportive of them because of the work they put in and then we try to work a lot with them to how we can find them and how they can connect more with each other and the same with Sam [Kerr].".

He has found a unique way to make Shaw and Lavelle work together, despite the fact that they appear to have overlapping skill sets when it comes time for USWNT head coach Emma Hayes to slot them into her lineup. The pair often play just behind Kerr, an out-and-out striker, and assume the role of strikers themselves while balancing their creative tendencies. They have filled in some gaps along the way -- Kerr, for example, ranks third in the league with 9.67 expected goals since returning to the NWSL on July 16 but has scored just four times. Kerr does, though, have four assists in 17 games, one fewer than Shaw and one more than Lavelle over that span.

In a recent development, the connection between Lavelle and Shaw has offered Gotham a level of dynamism that has been missing in their attack at times over the years, even as they racked up title after title. It helps that the two have enjoyed working alongside each other, the 21-year-old Shaw in particular taking inspiration from Lavelle, a decade her senior.

"I think her movement is some of the best in the world, honestly," Shaw said after that September win over the Stars. "She's able to make stretch runs, drag players. She attracts so many players, opening up space for other players to get on the ball and then getting on the second one, I think, is one of her strengths and is something I'm trying to replicate off of her. I think she's just incredibly smart in soccer knowledge.".

Industry observers note that for each of them, a return to fitness after small injuries in the final weeks of the regular season comes not a moment too soon. Kerr's inconsistency is not the only attacking glitch they will need to overcome -- Jordyn Dudley will miss the postseason with a foot fracture she sustained last month, her impressive rookie season coming to a close with four goals and three assists. Lavelle and Shaw will be particularly useful against the Reign, whose defensive qualities continue to be a strength.

In a recent development, shaw has become the focal point of Gotham's reinvention in recent years, but Amoros' side has added experienced options in a wide variety of positions since the 2023 championship. The vast majority of Gotham's likely starters on Sunday will have joined the club after the 2023 playoff run, a steady stream of notable players signing themselves up since. Ann-Katrin Berger, the 2024 goalkeeper of the year, made the move not long after Davidson and Lavelle did, and European champion Jess Carter followed right after. Midfielder Jaelin Howell, who has been in and around the USWNT, was recruited in time for the 2025 season, and Shaw joined months later. Left back Guro Reiten has two goals and six assists since making her club debut in April, while Kerr made the move at roughly the same time as midfielder Denise O'Sullivan, a two-time NWSL champion with the North Carolina Courage.

Gotham's reinvention is constant, the core evolving each and every season. It is a unique route to the top, but in another season of change, they found the consistency they have been chasing since the 2023 championship. The underdog label has well and truly been shed, the team chasing another tag entirely -- a third championship would put them level with the Portland Thorns as the most successful team in the league's history.

Aston Villa could reportedly be tempted to part ways with Boubacar Kamara next summer, but only if an interested club puts an enormous offer on the table.

The 26-year-old has become one of Unai Emery’s most trusted midfielders and remains a key part of Villa’s intends.

However, interest from Chelsea and other major clubs has increased in recent weeks, forcing the Midlands side to consider what level of bid might eventually make them reconsider their position.

According to Football Insider, former Aston Villa chief executive Keith Wyness believes an offer of around £80million could make the club seriously think about selling Kamara.

Villa are not actively looking to move the France international on, and his importance has only increased this season. Kamara has started every Premier League game so far and leads Villa for defensive contributions per 90 minutes.

Chelsea have emerged as one of the clubs most interested in the midfielder, with their recruitment team assessing whether a future deal could be possible.

Sources indicate that villa remain in a strong negotiating position, though. Kamara is under contract until 2030, meaning they have no need to accept anything below a premium fee.

According to recent reports, kamara is not simply a defensive midfielder who breaks up play. He is comfortable receiving the ball under pressure, reads danger exceptionally well and gives Emery’s side balance when they commit players forward.

A CaughtOffside report recently noted that Villa are monitoring Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia, while also highlighting growing interest in Kamara from Inter Milan, Arsenal and Liverpool.

That wider interest strengthens Villa’s hand. The bigger issue is squad depth. With Amadou Onana sidelined long term, losing Kamara would leave a major hole in midfield and force Villa straight back into the market.

For that reason, a January sale should be considered almost impossible.

Next summer could be different if Chelsea or another club arrives with a huge offer, but Villa should only entertain a deal if the money is significant enough to fund a genuine replacement and strengthen other areas.

Kamara is too important to sell cheaply. If someone wants him, £80m feels like the right starting point.

"Zirkzee was wanted by Juventus. Zirkzee was wanted by Fiorentina over the summer transfer window. Industry observers note that "For Zirkzee, there was also an opportunity at Everton in the final minutes of the summer transfer window, but it didn't happen because of one reason: the deal collapsing, also with Monaco and that Balogun story at the end of the summer window. It has been revealed that "Joshua Zirkzee is going to have a conversation with Mauricio Pochettino. Recent findings suggest that "Zirkzee has wanted to go and play for some time now, not only in the recent weeks or months; Zirkzee wants to go because he wants to play. He loves Man United, but he feels he's not a regular starter, and he wants to play football. He wants to play regular football.

"So let's see what kind of opportunities will arrive on the table. But I will not be surprised to see Joshua Zirkzee on the move in January, unless Mauricio Pochettino can sort the situation with the boy and clarify the situation.".

While it's clear that Zirkzee wasn't in the prepares of Michael Carrick at Old Trafford, it remains to be seen if Pochettino has the same feeling with him.

The Netherlands international had a strong pre-season before being sidelined by Carrick, but he has scored twice in his last four appearances for the club, all coming off the substitutes bench, against Como and Aston Villa.

In a recent development, his technical qualities are unmatched in the squad, and if Pochettino is capable of getting him to link with the rest of the forwards in the squad, then he could be a really useful member of the squad. But if he doesn't want to be at the club, then there is no point keeping him around.

With that said, Man Utd's squad is far too thin right now, and they cannot afford to let him leave in January without replacing him first. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki went from being serenaded with a chorus of “world’s No 1” to making a bizarre blunder that denied Unai Emery’s side a third successive Premier League victory.

The Villa manager, however, preferred to focus on a string of crucial saves from Suzuki rather than the uncharacteristic mistake that allowed Fulham to collect a deserved point.

It all went wrong for the hosts just after the hour mark in a match where Fulham provided more than a few scares before finding the net in unexpected fashion.

Alex Iwobi, who had been denied superbly by a Suzuki save just moments earlier, swung in a corner. It was right on top of the Villa goalkeeper, who tried to keep it out but only succeeded in fumbling it over the line. A frantic attempt to gather the ball was in vain and goal-line technology confirmed the goal stood.

Zion Suzuki drops Alex Iwobi's corner and Fulham are level! 🫨 https://t.co/KwLFMRpKqk.

Suzuki appeared to have been put off by the presence of Fulham’s Shea Charles, but Emery refused to single out the player for criticism.

Recent findings suggest that “I prefer to speak about the saves that he made,” the Villa manager remarked. “This is part of football. I think he played fantastically and he is doing a lot of saves so he can make one mistake. It is part of football. We can be mature about this.

In a recent development, “I still want to see consistency. Over the last five Premier League matches, we are winning three and drawing two. It’s not bad but with our poor start it’s not enough.

“We have to change our mind quickly for Tuesday against Barcelona. We want to test ourselves at this level.”.

Villa go to the Nou Camp with a 100 per cent Champions League record to their name this season. But they will need to improve on Saturday evening’s performance to get a result in Spain.

As well as Suzuki’s error, a 14th-minute penalty miss from John McGinn also proved costly.

Sources indicate that it was awarded after Leon Goretzka, making his full league debut for Villa, saw his header hit Sander Berge’s raised hand. Nobody appealed at the time but referee Sam Barrott was sent to the touchline monitor by VAR to review the incident and gave the spot-kick.

In a recent development, mcGinn’s attempt, however, hit the crossbar and the chance to take an early lead went begging. The Villa captain seemed a strange choice to take the spot-kick as he has only ever scored one career penalty, but Emery defended the choice, saying: “We analysed the penalty takers in the squad and it was McGinn here.”.

It has been revealed that penalty MISSED! John McGinn hits the bar 💥 https://t.co/2kBYkYA2BY.

Nicolas Jackson was on hand to ease Villa’s nerves before the break, though. the Villa manager had mentioned before the game that the striker’s goalscoring capability meant he was capable of matching the likes of Harry Kane. His assessment was backed up by Jackson scoring the opening goal, after 40 minutes, which summed up the striker in one moment of pure power combined with agility.

Collecting Johan Manzambi’s superbly weighted pass, Jackson forced his way past two defenders before sliding in the goal that put Villa ahead.

Emery’s touchline celebrations stated it all as the Senegal forward continues to flourish under the man who knew how to get the best out of him at Villarreal.

Nicolas Jackson scores his fifth league goal in five games! 🔥 https://t.co/W0xmFtW1Gt.

Suzuki has also flourished under Emery and he kept Villa in the game with some superb saves.

When Antonee Robinson crossed for Gonzalo Garcia, his step over allowed Oscar Bobb in for what looked like his second goal in successive games. But Suzuki pulled off a stunning fingertip save. That had Villa supporters singing: “Zion Suzuki, the world’s No 1”.

Robinson put in another cross and Suzuki got a touch that was enough to make Garcia put his shot wide. Villa were living dangerously and the Japanese goalkeeper made another outstanding stop to keep out Iwobi’s header. But then it all went wrong for Suzuki when he fumbled Iwobi’s corner.

That allowed Fulham’s recent revival under manager, Alvaro Arbeloa, to continue – they now have seven points from their past three games.

It has been revealed that “We spoke at half-time about what we had to do,” Arbeloa remarked. “If you want to win a game you have to fight and I think we have to believe in our way, we’ve shown we can beat anyone in the way that we play but we have to be aggressive.

“We created so many chances and at the end it’s one point in a difficult stadium. I’m so happy with the second half because of the way we played, this is the team that we want to be.”.

After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

“If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery said. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”.

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

According to recent reports, “It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa noted. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”.

Former USMNT goalkeeper Tim Howard has named the 'brilliant' manager he'd love to see replace Mauricio Pochettino, going as far as to claim he would be a better fit for the USA than Pep Guardiola.

That's quite the statement from the 47-year-old, considering the Spaniard's glittering CV. Guardiola has lifted six Premier League titles during his time at Manchester City, while also collecting three Champions League crowns across spells with City and Barcelona.

When it comes to the greatest managers in world football, few can hold a candle to him, and he remains the highest-ranked among those still active in the game.

But Howard, who earned 121 caps for his country, isn't convinced Guardiola would be the 'right fit' for a USA side boasting the likes of Folarin Balogun, Antonee Robinson and Christian Pulisic. Instead, he's thrown a major curveball by backing a very different candidate, with his choice likely to raise more than a few eyebrows.

It has been revealed that howard has caused a huge uproar after advocating for his former Everton manager, Roberto Martinez, to be the next USMNT coach. He was speaking to Landon Donovan on the Unfiltered Soccer podcast about possible upcoming coaches for the USMNT. “Roberto Martinez, he's the most brilliant football mind I've ever been around,” Howard stated.

Sources indicate that “So I would say this, and I hope people at U.S. Soccer will hear this. I honestly, hand on heart, think you're absolutely absurd, U.S. Soccer, if he is not your top one or two candidates. Do not pass Roberto Martínez by. Please don't. U.S Soccer, whether it's Dan [Helfrich] or JT [Baton] or Gooch [Oguchi Onyewu], all the guys I know, please.

Sources indicate that he has got to be top two candidates. And for me he's one. “Think about this. He took Wigan, by the way, Wigan were a bunch of farmers. Like Wigan were terrible. They were terrible. He got them to over 500 passes in games on average, won the FA Cup against Manchester City. Okay? I know they got relegated. He then comes to Everton. We were a Moyes Everton team, and we had a blueprint, and it worked and it was successful. He came to us and changed our entire identity. Our identity before was really good, sure. He just changed it and made us different.".

He continued: “His ability to teach players to get tactical. His ability to get tactical awareness from players. At Everton, let’s say you're his best right-winger. If you can't do it, he’ll get the second best guy and that player will thrive in his system, which will make you better because you don’t want to lose your place. He's just brilliant.

Recent findings suggest that “Oh, then by the way, he coached two massive national teams, Belgium with their golden generation, major players, and Portugal. And by the way, he handled Ronaldo. And if anyone thinks Ronaldo's easy to handle, ask their most recent manager. He guided it expertly. He knows World Cups. He knows club football. He knows players. It's a no-brainer for me. And you can see by the way I'm speaking.”.

It has been revealed that howard and Martínez worked together at Everton from 2013 to 2016. The Spaniard started off his managerial career in Wales with Swansea, and worked for English clubs like Wigan and Everton.

Recent findings suggest that he then coached Belgium in the 2018 and 2022 World Cups, and Euro 2020. He won them their first ever third place medal in the 2018 World Cup, but notably failed to get the best out of the country's golden generation, with the likes of a prime Kevin De Bruyne and Romelu Lukaku seemingly destined for silverware.

Recent findings suggest that the 53-year-old coached Portugal in the 2026 World Cup, and helped them win the Nations League over his home country Spain in 2025. But whether he really ranks among the top coaches remains up for debate - he is heavily criticised because his possession-heavy style often feels slow, overly cautious, and unable to turn elite talent into decisive wins in major tournaments.

He also often seems to lack a 'Plan B', which means rivals find it easy to read his next move. That's a far cry from Pochettino's reign, as the new Red Devils boss is excellent at finding new ways of getting the best out of his team, making him a smart long-term project manager.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aimar Blázquez scored twice from Rioja assists as Valencia beat Tavernes 6-0 at Mestalla, where the hosts were officially the away side. The win follows a 0-3 defeat to Real Madrid and takes Valencia into the second round.

Valencia cruised past Tavernes in the Copa del Rey on Tuesday 10 November 2026. The tie was played at the Estadio de Mestalla, yet Valencia were officially the away side in their own stadium. The RFEF had granted Tavernes’ request to stage the match there.

In a recent development, raba opened the scoring in the first minute, with Blázquez providing the assist. Raba then turned provider for Duro in the 11th minute. Rioja added the third in the 19th minute after a pass from Martinez. A fourth goal arrived through Elliott in the 23rd minute.

Tavernes goalkeeper Mainar kept the margin there three minutes into the second half. He saved a header from Blázquez, who had been set up by Raba. The number 37 struck in the 57th minute and again in the 69th. Danjuma replaced him after 70 minutes, when Gayà also came on for Rioja.

Three players were booked. Ugrinic was cautioned in the ninth minute and Montilla of Tavernes in the 22nd. Rioja picked up a yellow card in the 49th minute.

Tavernes came closest to a goal when Erik struck the post after a short corner. EFE described the visitors as a sixth-tier club and reported that close to 40 coaches carried their fans to Mestalla. Their municipal ground was not fit for the tie. Mestalla is in its final season before the move to Nou Mestalla.

In a recent development, A 9pm start had been planned for the tie. Every Copa del Rey match scheduled for that day was called off by the RFEF, and this one was among them.

Tavernes reached the first round through the two-legged preliminary round against UD Maracena. The first leg was played at the CD Maracena ground on Sunday 27 September 2026. The two sides drew 1-1 and 0-0.

In a recent development, for Valencia, the Real Madrid loss had itself followed a 1-0 win over Elche and a 1-2 defeat to Villarreal. #13721. Industry News: 20 Greatest Scottish Players in Football History [Ranked]

Industry News: 20 Greatest Scottish Players in Football History [Ranked]

📅 04 May 2024 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1823 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Givemesport

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For a proud nation of just five and a half million, Scotland has a remarkable record of producing footballers who have gone on to make their mark at the very highest level of the game.
  • Sources indicate that they are also a country with an incredible history too.
  • Scotland's two most famous club sides, the Old Firm, Rangers and Celtic, are steeped in history too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For a proud nation of just five and a half million, Scotland has a remarkable record of producing footballers who have gone on to make their mark at the very highest level of the game.

Sources indicate that they are also a country with an incredible history too. Along with the "Auld Enemy" England, Scotland are the joint oldest national team in the world, due to their participation in the world's first international football match when facing the Three Lions at Hamilton Crescent on the 30th of November 1872, a fixture that in commemoration of the occasion took place every year until 1989.

Scotland's two most famous club sides, the Old Firm, Rangers and Celtic, are steeped in history too. In terms of titles, Rangers are the second most successful club in the world and were also the first British team to reach a European final, falling short to Fiorentina in the 1961 Cup Winners' Cup Final. As for Celtic, they went one step further in the 1966/67 season under legendary manager Jock Stein, becoming the first British side to win the European Cup, defeating Inter Milan in the final.

But what about some of the sport's best players? Those to have donned the dark blue shirt with the most distinction. With that in mind, here are the 20 best Scottish footballers in history.

20 Greatest Scottish Players in Football History (20-12).

Sources indicate that despite standing at just 5'7", footballers don't come much more intimidating than Dave Mackay. Nicknamed Football's Braveheart, Mackay had the career that he dreamed of as a boyhood Heart of Midlothian supporter, ending the club's 48-year wait for a major honour by winning an incredible seven trophies over nine seasons, including a record-breaking Scottish league championship in 1957/58.

Industry observers note that mackay then moved to Tottenham Hotspur and swiftly established himself as an integral member of the side that saw success in the early 1960s. Indeed, many have referred to Mackay as “the heartbeat” of Spurs’ double-winning season in 1961.

The tenacious midfielder won the English top division for a second time in 1969, this time with Derby County, with his performances that season seeing him named Football Writers Association’s Player of the Year. His success with the Rams continued, as he led the club to the title in 1975, this time as manager. His achievements in both his playing and coaching career saw Mackay inducted into both the English and Scottish Hall of Fame.

The only name in the top 10 from the 21st century, Andrew Robertson, has asserted himself as one of the finest players in his position of the Premier League era. Robertson first made a name for himself at Dundee United, putting in a string of impressive performances that saw him named PFA Scotland Young Player of the Year and rewarded with his first senior Scotland cap, whilst still just a teenager.

In 2017, Robertson followed in the footsteps of several Scottish football icons in joining Liverpool and soon became an irreplaceable part of Jurgen Klopp’s team, reaching the Champions League in his first season, a competition they won the following campaign. In 2019/20, after coming close the previous year, Robertson won the Premier League, and in 2021/22 he was part of the team that won the FA Cup and Carabao Cup. Now 32, Robertson has served as captain of the Scotland National Team since 2018, becoming the nation's most capped player in 2026.

John Grieg is one of football’s true one-club men. A fellow left-back, Greig joined Rangers at 17, and went on to make a staggering 755 official appearances for the club across his 17-year senior playing career. During his time at Ibrox, Grieg helped end an unwanted 35-year record of losing finals to Old Firm foe Celtic, when Rangers triumphed 3-0 in the replay of the 1963 Scottish Cup final. This was one of six Scottish Cups that Greig, along with an impressive five League Championships.

In his role as captain, Grieg was a leading figure in the club’s recovery following the Ibrox disaster in 1971. The following year, Greig captained the club to their first European silverware as the Light Blues lifted the European Cup Winners’ Cup with a 3-2 win over Dynamo Moscow in Barcelona. Greig captained his country on 15 occasions, most notably in Scotland’s famous 3-2 win in 1967 over England at Wembley, their first since winning the World Cup the previous year. At the turn of the millennium, Greig was named “The Greatest Ever Ranger” and now serves as a life president of the club.

Recent findings suggest that what Grieg is to Rangers, Billy McNeill is to Celtic. Nicknamed ‘Cesar’, McNeill was the lynchpin and captain of Jock Stein’s famous Celtic team that won nine consecutive Scottish League Championships, as well as seven Scottish Cups and six League Cups in that period.

McNeill’s crowning moment, however, came in May 1967, when he captained Celtic to the European Cup with a 2-1 victory over Inter Milan at the Estadio Nacional in Lisbon. This feat saw Celtic become the first British team to win the competition, and in turn gave McNeill the honour of being the first British man to lift the European Cup.

The defender ended his playing career with a club-record 822 appearances over an illustrious 18-year playing career. McNeill went on to enjoy an impressive managerial career too, first with Aberdeen, where he was succeeded by a certain Alex Ferguson, before returning to Celtic to take over from the great Stein. Peter Swales (Chairman of Man City in 1989), said of the icon:.

"If ever a man was made for a specific club, it was Billy McNeill and Glasgow Celtic. His heart was always at Parkhead.".

It has been revealed that another star of the famous ‘Lisbon Lions’ side, the name given to the 1967 European Cup-winning Celtic team, is Jimmy Johnson. Standing at just 5’4”, Johnson was famed for incredible speed and low centre of gravity which allowed him to weave his way beyond opponents, giving him his nickname, ‘Jinky’. Once he was off, he was impossible to stop.

Like McNeill, Johnson was part of Stein’s team that won nine consecutive league championships. It was in 1967, the year of their European Cup success, that Johnson came third in the voting for the Ballon d’Or. The tricky winger scored 129 goals for The Hoops and in 2002 was named the club’s greatest ever player.

Having started his career with Partick Thistle, Alan Hansen enjoyed incredible success after making the £100,000 move to Liverpool in 1977. The Scotsman established himself as one of Liverpool's greatest ever players in an incredible 14-year spell. The ball-playing centre-back represented the Reds on 620 occasions, playing an integral role for a side that dominated English football in the 1980s. He won 25 trophies with the club, including eight league titles and three European Cups.

While he had great success at club level, his international career wasn't as fruitful. He played just 26 games for his country, with the formidable partnership of Miller and McLeish often preferred. Despite his lack of impact on an international stage, he is still regarded as one of the greatest centre-backs in football history and one of the finest players Scotland have ever produced.

One of the only players on this list to have played exclusively outside of Scotland, Billy Bremner is a member of both the English and Scottish Hall of Fame, and it’s easy to understand why. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest midfielders of his generation and was central to Leeds United’s most successful period, captaining the club to English First Division titles in 1968/69 and 1973/74, as well as winning the League Cup in 1968 and the FA Cup in 1972.

Industry observers note that bremner is second in the West Yorkshire club’s all-time appearance makers, with 772 over 16 years, and having played just one match fewer than the legendary Jack Charlton. In 1970, Bremner was named the FWA Football of the Year and was voted Leeds United’s greatest player of all time. The combative midfielder also earned over 50 caps for Scotland and was captain during their 1974 World Cup campaign.

Better known to younger audiences for his stern critique of the modern game on punditry panels, Graeme Souness was an equally fiery footballer during his playing days, although one of the best of his generation.

It has been revealed that known for his tough tackling and leadership, Souness was at the heart of the incredible success Liverpool experienced under Bob Paisley. During his time on Merseyside, Souness won an unprecedented five league titles in six seasons, as well as the European Cup just four months after joining the club. The midfielder won a further two European Cups in 1980/81 and 1983/84 before departing for Serie A with Sampdoria, winning the Coppa Italia in his first season.

Undoubtedly one of the most naturally gifted footballers Scotland has ever produced, Jim Baxter, at his peak was a joy to behold. Glasgow-born, Baxter joined Rangers in 1960, where he remained for five seasons, displaying his quality and importance to the team that won the Scottish League First Division three times, the Scottish Cup three times, and the Scottish League Cup on four occasions. In 1965, in what was his final year before departing for England, Baxter, nicknamed ‘Slim Jim’ for his agility and effortless play, came 13th in the voting for the Ballon d’Or. Sir Alex Ferguson even noted of Baxter:.

In a recent development, "Arguably the best player to play in Scottish football. He had touch, balance, vision and just this wonderful aura.".

Industry observers note that in Scotland’s infamous 3-2 win against England in 1967, Baxter starred, tormenting the then-World Champions with keepie-uppies whilst waiting for teammates to find space. Injuries and addiction saw his career curtailed and by 1970, aged just 31, Baxter unveiled his retirement.

One of the great strikers in the sport’s history, Denis Law twice broke the British transfer record, first with his move from his academy side Huddersfield Town to Manchester City, and then again in 1962 when he returned to England from Torino to join Manchester United. It was at United where Law enjoyed the best years of his career, forming of the greatest attacking trios in English football history alongside George Best and Bobby Charlton, and winning the First Division in 1965 and 1967.

Law spent 11 years at Old Trafford, finding the net on 237 occasions, a total that makes him the third-highest goal scorer in Manchester United's history. Moreover, Law holds the club record for the most goals scored in a single season with 43, and with 30 goals is also Scotland’s joint-highest scorer in their history.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: Denis Law remains to this day the only Scottish player to have ever won the Ballon d’Or, doing so in 1964.

Kai Havertz leads the Premier League in offsides as Arsenal pile up infractions in 1-0 win over Hull City

💡 Key Takeaways
  • LONDON -- Though there was some to-ing and fro-ing as to the order in which the offenses should be considered, it seemed fitting that what would have been Arsenal's best scoring chance of the first half of their 1-0 win over Hull City was wiped out for an offside.
  • Sometimes the opponent is even willing to offer them a helping hand.
